title: How Does Water Work? Floating, Sinking and Steam
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Gizmo the robot, and welcome to Gizmo Explains!
I love asking, how does that work? Today we're going to explore wonderful water.
We'll explore five cool things. Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
When my antenna lights up, it means I have an idea!

lines: Here's a clue: a boat does it, and so does a rubber duck! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
When something sits in water, the water pushes up on it from below.
If the push is strong enough to hold it up, it floats! Boats are shaped to let water push up a lot.
Can you lie back and float, like a boat on the water?
What pushes up on a floating boat?
One more time, nice and loud: FLOATING!
Big, heavy ships float too, because their wide shape spreads out on the water.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: a rock does it when you drop it in a pond! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
A rock is small, but it's very heavy for its size.
The water can't push up hard enough to hold it, so down, down it goes to the bottom!
Can you sink down slowly, down to the floor?
Does a leaf sink or float?
It floats! A leaf is very light for its size.
One more time, nice and loud: SINKING!
Try it at bath time with a grown-up: which toys float, and which ones sink?
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it can be hard, wet, or floaty! Can you guess?
Here comes: Ice, Water and Steam!
How does it work? Let's find out!
Water can be three things: solid ice, runny water, or floaty steam.
Warm up ice, and it melts into water. Heat water a lot, and it turns into steam!
Can you be stiff like ice, then wiggly like water, then float like steam?
What happens when water gets very hot?
Let's say it together: ICE, WATER AND STEAM!
One more time, nice and loud: ICE, WATER AND STEAM!
Steam is very hot, so only grown-ups use the kettle. We just watch from far away.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's a glass of ice water that gets wet on the outside! Can you guess?
Now let's look at: Cold Glass!
How does it work? Let's find out!
The air around us has tiny bits of water in it that we can't see.
When that air touches a cold glass, it cools down and turns into little drops!
Can you wiggle your fingers like tiny drops on a glass?
Where do the drops come from?
From the air! Not from inside the glass.
Let's say it together: COLD GLASS!
One more time, nice and loud: COLD GLASS!
That's why grass is wet with dew on a cool morning. It's the same trick!
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's on the ground after the rain, splash! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
When the sun shines on a puddle, it warms the water.
The water turns into a gas we can't see, and floats up into the sky. Bye-bye, puddle!
Can you float up, up, up like water going into the sky?
Up into the air! Then it helps make clouds.
One more time, nice and loud: PUDDLE!
Wet clothes on a sunny day dry the same way. The water floats away!
Now we know how it works. Great job!

recap: Wow, we learned so much! Let's remember.
Water pushes up to make things float.
Water can be ice, water, or steam.
Cold glasses get drops from the air.
And puddles float up into the sky!
outro: Which one was your favorite? Keep asking, how does that work?
Bye, friends! See you next time on Gizmo Explains!
